content: A disabled millennial writer reflects on the growing isolation faced by disabled people in Britain, highlighting new research from the charity Scope which reveals that nearly half of working-age disabled people — approximately 3 million individuals — report feeling chronically lonely. Set against the broader context of Britain being labeled "the loneliness capital of Europe" by the Office for National Statistics, with weak social connections and young people particularly affected, the article underscores that disabled people face an even more severe epidemic of loneliness, where basic aspects of daily life such as going to work, socializing, or simply interacting with others cannot be taken for granted, pointing not just to emotional loneliness but to stark physical isolation.
